subject: Clarify output & training consent clauses + fallback policy — evidence request
messages:
From: Claire Hudson <claire.hudson@nimbus-systems.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@nimbus-systems.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus - redlines on output / training / fallback policy (attached)

Hi Grace & Laura,

Thanks for the draft MSA + order form. Our legal team (attached) has pushed back on a few items that are material for us:

- Output ownership: we need explicit assignment for customer-specific models built from our data, or at minimum an exclusive license for productization of outputs tied to our dataset.
- Training & data use: we need a scoped opt-in for any model retraining; no automatic use of telemetry or customer prompts for training.
- Feedback license: any logging or feedback used to improve models should be limited to aggregate, non-attributable use unless we opt in.
- Fallback policy: we need clarity on what happens if your hosted model is unavailable — in particular whether Redwood can route to a different (larger/smaller) variant and whether that triggers additional rights.

Please see attached redlines (Nimbus_Redlines_20270419.docx). Can you confirm what evidence you can provide (audit logs, evals, telemetry retention) to support the training/feedback controls? We also need a timeline for when Redwood can present an updated redline.

We'd prefer to keep this light-touch — 1–2 business days for a commercial response, and then legal-level redline the same week if possible.

Thanks,
Claire Hudson
Director, Partnerships (contracting lead)
Nimbus Systems
[Attachment: Nimbus_Redlines_20270419.docx]

Subject: Re: Nimbus - redlines on output / training / fallback policy (attached)

Claire — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Looping Laura and Ben for legal + sales alignment.

Quick commercial answers so you have them up front:
- Output ownership: our default is customer ownership of generated outputs (you own any specific content you provide and any final artifacts generated for you), but the order form needs to capture productization rights for customer-trained artifacts. We'll propose a narrow carveout for customer-owned artifacts used to build a "customer model" variant.
- Training & data use: we can agree to an explicit opt-in for retraining using customer data/telemetry. If you don't opt in, we will not include identifiable customer prompts or files in training corpora.
- Feedback license: we can limit feedback to aggregate, non-attributable use by default; we'll add a clause for explicit opt-in for any attribution or finer-grained telemetry use.
- Fallback policy: we have a routing policy that prefers the pinned model; if pinned capacity is unavailable we can route to a compatible variant. We know you care about parity (latency/cost/feature parity) — we'll propose language that ensures any fallback variant cannot produce materially different rights outcomes (i.e., fallback won't change output ownership or grant Redwood broader rights).

I'll attach a one-page commercial response and ask Laura to follow up with legal redlines. We'll aim to get you an updated draft today for commercial terms and legal redlines by EOD tomorrow.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Claire, Grace — attaching legal redlines and a short playbook for the evidence Nimbus requested. High level: we can accept scoped customer ownership and an opt-in training/feedback regime with clear operational controls.

Key redline items (summary):
1) Output ownership: add a section in the order form that (a) confirms customer ownership of "Customer Outputs" (as defined), (b) allows Redwood to retain ephemeral model weights used only for serving but forbids reuse for general model retraining without explicit order-form opt-in. This addresses productization while protecting Redwood's model IP.

2) Training & feedback: add an opt-in checkbox on the order form ("Customer elects to allow Redwood to use Customer Data and Telemetry for Model Training") plus a telemetry-sampling cap (e.g., sample <= 0.5% of prompts unless higher rate is mutually agreed). If the customer opts out, technical controls will ensure KV caches and prefix caches are excluded from any persistent corpora.

3) Feedback license: limit to "aggregate, de-identified feedback for quality improvements" unless a separate mutual license is executed. Add auditability: Redwood will provide quarterly summaries of feedback-derived changes, plus a one-time evidence package (sample audit logs, eval diffs) within 5 business days upon written request during negotiation.

4) Fallback routing & model variant parity: define "fallback" as temporary routing to a compatible variant that preserves the order form's rights. Fallback cannot trigger additional rights (e.g., it cannot change output assignment or enable training use unless the customer opted in). Also propose an SLA clause that describes notification windows (30 minutes for cross-variant fallback, written post-mortem within 48 hours for capacity incidents).

Attachments: Redwood_Legal_Redlines_20270420.docx (redlines embedded), and a short evidence checklist (audit log sample, token-level retention policy summary, eval snapshot).

Questions for Nimbus before we finalize:
- Is the sampling cap acceptable as a technical safeguard? If not, propose an alternative (e.g., sampling by endpoint or endpoint-level opt-in).
- Do you need additional controls around derivative productization (for example, an explicit embargo on selling a customer-derived model to third parties)?

I'll circulate tracked redlines in the shared Drive folder and will mark items that require further commercial negotiation (pricing for customer model variants, any escrow requests).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
